title: What If an Immortal Snail Was Chasing You?
lines: Gus has a billion dollars, and he's running away from a snail.
It's nine in the morning in the garden, and the deal is simple.
He keeps the money. But a snail that can't die will follow him forever, and one touch means game over.
His wife laughs. It's a snail. His neighbor steps right over it. Just walk away.
And they've got a point. The fastest snail ever timed took two minutes to go thirteen inches.
Gus takes one step and the snail needs four minutes to catch up.
He walks almost five hundred times faster than it crawls.
So why can't Gus sleep at night?
You see, Gus has to stop. He eats. He naps. He sleeps. The snail never does.
It's like a dripping tap. One drop is nothing, but leave it for a week and it fills a whole bathtub.
Every night Gus sleeps, the snail gets eighty-seven yards closer.
That's two hundred and sixty yards a day, and fifty-four miles a year.
Luckily, Gus can win a whole day back with a three-minute walk.
And one flight across the ocean puts sixty-four years between them.
Unluckily, snails are very good at hitching a ride.
So Gus lands on a sunny beach with a billion dollars, one suitcase, and one very patient snail.
